description: Console startup is now persistent: the setup one-liner and the x5agent command both start the server detached, so closing SSH or the terminal never stops it, and re-running the same command kills the old server and starts a fresh one on the same port. x5agent --off stops every project server on the port.
features: Typing @ mid-word in Arabic opens the file picker; emails like mail@x never trigger it.
@file and /skill boundaries match between editor paint and server injection, including Arabic adjacency.
Browser downloads auto-move to Workspace/downloads; no empty folder hides the live view anymore.
Blue @file highlight keeps the same glyph widths as the text, so the caret no longer looks stuck inside a character.
The browser stays open: WSL idle-shutdown can no longer tear the live stack down mid-session.
Live downloads are bridged into the watched folder, so finished files always arrive in Workspace/downloads.
Files and folders inside downloads/ now show a delete button; the downloads folder itself can never be deleted.
Every model call (text, vision, STT, TTS, image) now routes AIP/1 records through the same interpreter path as the agent loop; legacy connections behave exactly as before.
Scheduled/trigger skill generation also falls back to the legacy engine for legacy-configured models, so task creation works with either record type.
Armed triggers keep working after a restart (watchers re-arm automatically).
Schedules accept seconds (every 30s) and invalid repeat patterns are rejected with a clear error.
Editing a scheduled task or trigger regenerates its skill so it never goes stale.
Library page triggers (manage_triggers) now create a Skill from the task plus the last-10 chat, arm the matching browser trigger, and run the Skill once when the page event fires.
One entry owns one library trigger plus one Skill: create one entry per event for a dedicated Skill each on the same site.
The library supports many concurrent triggers at once (up to 100; the project caps at 50) plus several OR events inside one trigger.
Trigger executions now run in their own hidden session instead of the main chat; the session is deleted with the trigger.
Scheduled run sessions render like the main chat: rich text, Working steps with elapsed time, and copy/edit/regenerate/delete on every message.
The task skill arrives as a normal user message and follow-ups show the same Working block and action bars as the main session.
Completed tasks no longer show a Pause button; only active or paused tasks can toggle it.
Executions list redesigned with status chips, run time, open arrow, and output previews; floating task cards restyled with status edge strips.
Task follow-ups are sent raw with the skill seeded once in the branch history and the full main-chat context, so the session answers like a separate normal chat instead of repeating the task reply.
Execution context is now guaranteed: system prompt + memories + environment + skill-as-message + same tools, never chat history.
The main context lists every armed trigger with its task and how to manage it.
Scheduled run pages no longer show the task name on top, so they fit phones.
Opening a scheduled run auto-hides the floating Scheduled Tasks window.
Settings has a black Delete chat history button with the live message count and a loading spinner; it clears the main chat + its search index only — saved memories stay.
Project card in Settings redesigned with a cleaner repository + version layout.
Update check fixed: the description is back within its 500-char limit and the console version matches updates.json.
Default white buttons (Cancel / secondary actions) are now professional glass, matching the dashboard glass language; black and red buttons keep their look.
White buttons redesigned as light ovals (Change password, Delete chat history, Cancel): solid pill, dark text, gentle lift on hover.
Public link stays alive: the live stream survives Tailscale Funnel resets (proxy-safe SSE headers + 15s heartbeat) instead of dying with 502.
No more false logout over the public link: the page goes to login only when the session is proven expired, otherwise it reconnects by itself.
Reconnects fast after a funnel blip (1s/2s/5s backoff) and replays the latest snapshot on every redial.
Black boot splash with the Working ring-wave dots and wave brand text replaces all skeleton shimmer templates, including the agent chat placeholders.
The splash lifts only after all boot data is ready (live snapshot plus dashboard, charts, chat, plugins, skills, models, workspace, scheduler, gateway and settings first loads).
Page entrance replays on reveal, and a 15s watchdog guarantees the splash can never trap the screen when the backend is unreachable.
Balance card shows measured lifetime spend (per-request captured prices summed), e.g. $0.55 measured spend · 174 requests, instead of the empty connect-a-model state.
Daily cost charts use the same per-request sums, so charts and Balance always agree; older rows without a capture are priced from the cached table.
Boot splash never flashes on fast loads: it only appears when loading takes longer than a moment, otherwise the screen goes straight to data.
Boot reveal is a single animation: page content stays hidden until all data lands, then appears exactly once with its entrance - no multi-jump refresh.
Balance pricing also matches short custom model names to provider rates (gpt-4o-mini finds openai/gpt-4o-mini), so more requests measure a real dollar cost.
The setup one-liner and x5agent now start the console detached: safe to close SSH, same command restarts (old server killed, new one on 7777).
x5agent --off (alias x5agent-off) stops every project server on the port.
Server log lives in X5Agent/Data/logs/console.log for persistent runs.
